name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest listed electronics manufacturing services (EMS) company: smartphones (Q2 FY27 revenue +47%, volumes ex-Vivo guided ~32-33m units for FY27), TVs, home appliances (washing machines, fridges), lighting, security devices (CCTV), IT hardware (laptops/ tablets), camera modules and display modules through Chinese-technology JVs (Vivo India 51%, HKC, Longcheer, Chongqing Yuhai, Q Tech, Signify). Very low margins (EBITDA 2.7% in Q2 FY27) and high working-capital intensity; profits depend on PLI/ECMS subsidies, component cost pass-through and backward integration. Promoter holding 28.5%.

revenue_mix.geography: India (domestic brands) ~95% / exports small; approximate, model knowledge

revenue_mix.segment: Lighting, security, telecom, IT hardware, others

exposures.mechanism: Memory price spike raises mobile BOM; Dixon passes costs through (revenue +47% partly price-led) but with a lag, and market smartphone volumes fell 16% YoY. At ~3% EBITDA margin, -0.5pp margin from lag = EBITDA -15%, plus ~5% volume risk; persistence 0.3, EV/MCap ~1.0 => ~-5. Q2 EBITDA margin 2.7% (3.8% a year ago) is the live evidence.

evidence.note: Q2 FY27: revenue +47% to ~Rs21,800cr, PAT before NCI Rs411cr (-45%), EBITDA margin 2.7%; Vivo JV start slipped to Q4 FY27; stock +11% on 2 Nov

exposures.mechanism: Mobile PLI ended in FY26 (cited as a cause of the Q2 margin fall, -110bp). A successor/ECMS (component scheme) approval for Dixon's component JVs would restore ~0.5-1.0pp of mobile margin: +1 = expansion => EBITDA +20% x persistence 0.5 => ~+4 (shaded).
